basis: Proposal A for the generator check of the G4 pilot (python -m egw_experiments generator-check), put forward on 2026-10-07. NOT adopted: with this file no report certifies (status 'proposed'; exit 3, every per-tolerance result labelled non-certifying). Approval is the student's act: a decision record, then a copy of this profile with status 'approved' and an approval naming who approved it, that decision record and the date. It is presented before the execution authorisation.

Profile A is structural: never one scheduled interval behind. It applies the same three limits to the four pilot conditions: nominal at 11.2 msg/s (the 120 s and the 600 s runs), the load sweep at 10 and at 50 msg/s, and the soak at 11.2 msg/s.

max_overrun_events = 0. An overrun is an event published at or after the due time of the next scheduled instant, the state in which the run loop skips its sleep and catches up (egw_simulator/runner.py, pace_until). Zero means that no published event fell a full scheduled interval behind.

max_relative_lateness_ms = 20.0. (i) It is below the smallest gap between scheduled instants of every pilot condition (22.4 ms at 50 msg/s, 100 ms at 11.2 msg/s, 112 ms at 10 msg/s), so it implies zero overruns at every pilot rate. (ii) It is 2.05 times the worst relative lateness the check measures on the three sealed nominal-scenario runs of the G3 battery, at 11.2 msg/s on this host: 9.762 ms (nominal-r02), 5.407 ms (controller_restart-r03) and 7.958 ms (controller_restart-r04), 20,160 events with no overrun and every 1 s window as scheduled (docs/evidence/g3-battery-2026-10). That baseline is an engineering basis only and is non-citable. (iii) It is 2 % of the 1 s period of the 1 Hz samplers, so generator timing shifts no sampled observation.

max_span_deviation_ms = 20.0. The same bound on the first-to-last publish span against the scheduled span, so the run is neither stretched nor shortened. On the same three runs the deviation is at most 0.143 ms.

Costs. At 50 msg/s the scheduled gap (22.4 ms) is only 2.3 times the worst lateness seen at 11.2 msg/s, and no recorded run above 11.2 msg/s exists on this host. The soak has 40,320 events, so one host hiccup above 20 ms is not unlikely. A false NOT_SUSTAINED labels the run a pilot finding; the check changes no validity rule and no run's validity. A false SUSTAINED would mislead the pilot's feasibility finding.

Not proposed: alternative B (1000 ms lateness, 1000 ms span, overruns unbounded), set at the resolution of the 1 Hz samplers. It certifies a 0.9 s stall followed by catch-up, the failure the check exists to detect. A per-rate variant of A (the lateness limit equal to one scheduled interval: 100, 112 and 22.4 ms) is the other option left open.

What SUSTAINED under A would state: the client's publish calls kept the schedule over the whole run, within 20 ms of relative lateness and with no catch-up. It would not state what the broker received (paho queues QoS 1 messages locally beyond 20 in flight), nor an absolute lateness (the simulator does not record its schedule origin, so relative lateness omits a constant c >= 0).
